articles.title: The controversy surrounding Katie Zacharia continues: now she is accused of showing sensitive information on Instagram after her photo with Trump
articles.standfirst: A map could be seen whose appearance seemed to have been altered or blurred, something that did not take long to draw the attention of observers and political analysts
articles.summary: A map could be seen whose appearance seemed to have been altered or blurred, something that did not take long to draw the attention of observers and political analysts
articles.body:
Kate Zacharia's brief tenure as White House press secretary continues to generate headlines even after her departure . Just a few days after her abrupt dismissal, the former communications chief is once again at the center of controversy over a photograph posted on social media that has sparked all kinds of speculation.

Zacharia shared on Saturday an image alongside the President of the United States, Donald Trump, taken in the Oval Office . The snapshot had a tone of farewell and gratitude. "It has been an honor to work for him," she wrote alongside the post.

But the focus of numerous users was not on the protagonists of the photo, but on a detail that appeared on the presidential desk. In the image, a map could be seen whose appearance seemed to have been altered or blurred , something that did not take long to attract the attention of observers and political analysts.

The map that has raised alarms

Hours later, Zacharia posted another photograph on Instagram Stories, this time accompanied by her husband and her four children in the same setting. In that new image, the map was no longer visible .

From that moment on, speculation began. Some experts and activists claimed that the silhouette visible in the document matches the East Potomac Park area, one of the most emblematic spaces in Washington, D.C. and a place that has gained relevance due to the remodeling plans promoted by the Trump Administration.

The president announced last June his intention to renovate the golf course located in this park, which he described as a "deteriorated, worn-out, very dangerous, and obsolete" facility. However, the project is currently under judicial scrutiny following a lawsuit filed by the DC Preservation League.

Critics believe it reveals more than intended

The White House has insisted that there is still no final design for the renovation of the complex . Nevertheless, critics of the project believe that the map captured in the photograph could show that advanced plans are indeed already on the table.

Among the most critical voices is Alex Rosen, founder of the Save East Po platform, opposed to the proposed renovation. In statements to The Washington Post, he said that the noticeable details in the image match depictions that had already circulated previously of the park’s future design.

What was intended to be a simple farewell photo has thus turned into a new political controversy . An image, a blurry map, and a series of unanswered questions have once again put Zacharia in the media spotlight just days after leaving one of Washington's most high-profile positions.

articles.title: Where can you get the new Costco Fall Sundae? Price, calories and everything to know about the season special
articles.standfirst: The Costco Fall Sundae is available for fewer than three dollars
articles.summary: The Costco Fall Sundae is available for fewer than three dollars
articles.body:
Costco is giving shoppers another reason to visit its food court this fall with a Vanilla Apple Pie Sundae that combines creamy soft serve, apple pie filling and pieces of pastry for $2.99, as the seasonal dessert brings a familiar autumn favorite to the warehouse retailer's menu. The sundae recreates the flavors of apple pie served with ice cream, layering vanilla soft serve with sweet apple topping and chunks of pie crust. Its affordable price has already attracted attention online, with customers sharing their first impressions of the limited-time treat.

The Vanilla Apple Pie Sundae is available through Costco 's food court, although customers should check with their local warehouse to confirm whether it is being offered. Seasonal menu items can vary by location, and there is no guarantee that every store will stock the dessert but the sundae costs $2.99 per serving, placing it among Costco 's inexpensive food court treats. Shoppers looking for precise nutritional details should consult Costco 's current nutritional information to manage any health conditions.

How does it compare with Costco's other seasonal treats?

Early reviews have been largely positive, with customers praising the balance between the cold ice cream, apple filling and pastry pieces as one Reddit user described the combination as “room temperature warm mixed with ice cream,” highlighting the contrast between the topping and soft serve. Another customer called it “easily best one so far,” while a more detailed review praised the apple compote and the crunch provided by the pie crust. The same shopper said the dessert was slightly less sweet than Costco 's other regular sundaes. Others have praised the filling, describing it as thicker and better-tasting than a typical canned alternative, and highlighted the pastry pieces as another appealing feature, although not every reaction has been enthusiastic. One Reddit commenter offered a more critical view and said they felt the apple flavor was weak and wanted more cinnamon, suggesting that the dessert's appeal may depend on individual preferences. The new sundae follows other limited-time dessert offerings, including the Strawberry Shortcake Sundae and the return of Costco 's popular churro. The retailer has developed a following for affordable food court items, and seasonal additions give customers another reason to try something different. The churro's comeback also demonstrated how closely shoppers watch menu changes, with some customers disappointed that the returning version differed from the original treat they remembered. For fans of autumn flavors, the Apple Pie Sundae offers a straightforward alternative to buying an entire pie. At $2.99, it delivers a dessert inspired by a classic seasonal combination without requiring shoppers to visit a bakery. Customers hoping to try it should check availability at their local Costco before making a special trip.

articles.title: Powerball Winning Numbers: Results for Monday October 19 drawing for the $607 Million jackpot
articles.standfirst: The odds of winning the jackpot are 1 in 292,201,338
articles.summary: The odds of winning the jackpot are 1 in 292,201,338
articles.body:
P owerball players have another chance to win a life-changing fortune on Monday, October 19, as the estimated jackpot reaches $607 million following Saturday's drawing, prior to being subject to state and federal taxes.

Tickets cost $2 per play and are sold in 45 states, Washington, D.C. , Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands . In jurisdictions where online sales are permitted, players may also be able to purchase tickets digitally.

The odds of winning the Powerball jackpot are 1 in 292,201,338. Although players can win smaller prizes by matching fewer numbers, no number-selection strategy can guarantee a jackpot or improve the probability of a particular combination being drawn.

Players must meet the minimum legal age in the jurisdiction where they purchase a ticket. U.S. citizenship or residency is not required, so eligible international visitors can buy tickets while visiting participating jurisdictions, although tax obligations may apply to prizes.

The jackpot rolled over after the previous drawing failed to produce a ticket matching all six numbers. Players hoping to claim the top prize must match five white balls drawn from 1 to 69 and the red Powerball , selected from 1 to 26. The odds of winning the jackpot are 1 in 292,201,338.

The winning numbers for Monday's drawing have not been revealed yet, but Powerball drawings take place every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday. The results can be watched through the lottery's official drawing page, while previous drawings are available on its YouTube channel.

Check your ticket against the official results after Monday's drawing, and remember that the $607 million headline figure is an estimate rather than a guaranteed cash payout.

How much is the $607 million Powerball jackpot worth?

The advertised jackpot represents the annuity value, paid through an initial payment followed by 29 annual payments that increase by five percent each year as winners can instead choose a smaller lump-sum payment.

Both prize options are listed before taxes, and federal and state levies can substantially reduce the amount a winner ultimately receives, so the advertised jackpot should not be confused with the final take-home sum.

Players who prefer not to select their own numbers can use a Quick Pick , which allows a lottery terminal to generate a random combination, and the Power Play add-on costs an additional $1 and can multiply eligible non-jackpot prizes, depending on the multiplier drawn.

Powerball made headlines previously in December 2025 when a single ticket sold in Arkansas matched all six numbers to win an estimated $1.817 billion jackpot and the winner.

The winner could choose the advertised annuity of $1.817 billion but opted for a lump-sum payment of $834.9 million.

The prize ranked as the second-largest lottery jackpot ever won in the United States , and was the biggest Powerball prize of 2025.

articles.title: Super El Niño brings tropical surprises to California, from hammerheads to endangered turtles
articles.standfirst: There's a growing list of unusual marine encounters along Southern California's coast
articles.summary: There's a growing list of unusual marine encounters along Southern California's coast
articles.body:
California’s coastline is getting some unexpected visitors. Whale sharks, hammerhead sharks, manta rays and even a potentially deadly sea snake have appeared in waters where tropical marine life is far less common, as a powerful El Niño brings warmer ocean conditions farther north. The unusual encounters include a fish never before recorded in California , a venomous snake spotted on a Southern California beach and two endangered sea turtles that made history by laying eggs on the U.S. West Coast.

The developments have drawn attention from scientists, fishermen and beachgoers alike. According to a Reuters report published Oct. 17, the influx of tropical species is linked to an unusually strong El Niño, following an extended marine heat wave in the Pacific. But the spectacle comes with a warning: while some species benefit from warmer water, others may lose critical habitat as ocean conditions change.

A venomous sea snake makes a rare appearance

One of the most startling encounters occurred on the night of Sept. 11, when Jackie Aguilar and her family were walking along Crystal Cove State Beach in Orange County. They came across what appeared to be a yellow-bellied sea snake, a marine reptile whose venom can be dangerous to humans.

Certified marine naturalist Capt. Chad Steffen identified the animal as resembling the species, which has been exceptionally rare in California. The snake was reportedly seen near shore after spending much of its life in the open ocean. According to Reuters, experts have documented only six or seven confirmed sightings of yellow-bellied sea snakes in California. The previous confirmed sighting occurred during the 2015-16 El Niño.

The first turtle nested near Seal Beach on Sept. 16. Three days later, another laid eggs near Huntington Beach , roughly eight miles away. Olive ridley turtles typically nest in tropical regions, including Mexico and Central America. Their appearance in Southern California represents an extraordinary departure from the species' documented nesting range on the U.S. mainland Pacific coast.

Wildlife officials took special precautions to protect the eggs. Because hazardous surf and high tides threatened the nests, biologists collected more than 200 eggs on Sept. 25 and transferred them to the Aquarium of the Pacific in Long Beach for incubation. If the eggs hatch successfully, the hatchlings are expected to be released on the beaches where they were laid.

Unusual marine encounters

Scientists believe warmer sea surface temperatures associated with marine heat waves and the incoming El Niño may have contributed to the turtles' unexpected arrival. However, NOAA c autions that the precise reasons for the nesting events remain uncertain.

The unusual visitors extend well beyond fish and reptiles. Whale sharks, hammerheads, flying fish and manta rays have also been observed in California waters as warmer conditions encourage tropical species to venture north.

Meanwhile, whale watchers off Newport Beach experienced a remarkable encounter on Sept. 29, when a pod of approximately 10 to 13 killer whales swam alongside their boat during a Newport Landing Whale Watching cruise. The sighting added to a growing list of unusual marine encounters along Southern California's coast.

Although orcas are found throughout the world's oceans, their presence and movements vary by population and season. The warmer ocean conditions may influence where some animals travel, but the appearance of an individual pod does not, by itself, establish that El Niño caused its arrival.

What is El Niño doing to the Pacific?

El Niño is a naturally occurring climate pattern characterized by warmer-than-average sea surface temperatures across parts of the central and eastern tropical Pacific. It alters atmospheric circulation and ocean conditions, affecting weather and marine ecosystems across large areas.

Along California's coast, warmer water can allow tropical and subtropical species to travel farther north than they ordinarily would. The current influx follows an extended marine heat wave, making it difficult to attribute every unusual sighting to a single cause.

The effects are not all positive. Warm-water species may find new feeding opportunities, and sportfishing businesses can benefit from increased catches of tropical fish. Reuters reported that one Southern California fishing operator had caught approximately 5,000 yellowfin tuna this year, compared with just two during the same period a year earlier.

However, kelp forestswh, ich provide food and shelter for numerous marine species, depend on colder water. Scientists warn that prolonged warming can put these ecosystems under pressure, potentially affecting animals that rely on them. The result is a complicated picture: more opportunities to observe unusual wildlife, but also potential disruption to the established marine environment.

articles.title: What new Pepsi and Lay’s flavors are coming to the U.S. this holiday season?
articles.standfirst: From a vanilla and cream Pepsi to potato chips inspired by festive dishes, PepsiCo is preparing several new releases for the coming months.
articles.summary: From a vanilla and cream Pepsi to potato chips inspired by festive dishes, PepsiCo is preparing several new releases for the coming months.
articles.body:
You know the holiday season is getting closer when limited-edition products start appearing on store shelves. Pepsi and Lay’s know it, too, and are preparing five new Christmas-inspired flavors to win over consumers .

What new Pepsi and Lay’s flavors will be available?

Pepsi will kick off the season with Pepsi Vanilla & Cream and Pepsi Zero Sugar Vanilla & Cream , two varieties that combine the classic cola flavor with notes of vanilla and cream. Both will be available for a limited time starting in October, in 12-pack cans and 20-ounce bottles.

Lay’s, meanwhile, is betting on a special collection called Holi-LAY’S , featuring five varieties inspired by the flavors of holiday celebrations.

When will the new flavors hit stores?

The new products will arrive at U.S. retailers on different dates. Here is the expected schedule for trying each variety:

Late October: Lay’s Cheddar Scalloped-Style Potatoes and Roasted Holiday Turkey chips will arrive in stores. November 8: Lay’s Maple Bacon will begin rolling out to stores nationwide. December: The sweet varieties Lay’s Wavy Milk Chocolate and Wavy Dubai-Style Dark Chocolate-Covered Potato Chips are expected to arrive at select stores.

articles.title: Malibu’s Hollywood dream is under water as powerful tides batter celebrity homes
articles.standfirst: The latest damage is another blow to a luxury real estate market already struggling with uncertainty
articles.summary: The latest damage is another blow to a luxury real estate market already struggling with uncertainty
articles.body:
M alibu’s most exclusive oceanfront neighborhood is accustomed to Hollywood drama. But this time, the destruction is not happening on a movie set. Residents of Malibu Colony, the guard-gated enclave that has served as a retreat for celebrities, filmmakers and entertainment executives for generations, spent Saturday cleaning up after powerful waves and unusually high tides tore apart beachfront decks, ripped away staircases and sent seawater and sand into multimillion-dollar homes.

The aftermath of Tropical Storm Rachel left wood planks and rusty nails swirling in the surf, while shattered glass from blown-out windows littered battered outdoor decks. Other homeowners were left mopping up seawater inside their houses and prized tea rooms. The resident also warned that strong winds could trigger further power outages, adding to the difficulties facing a community still recovering from devastating wildfires.

The latest damage is more than a cleanup problem. It is another blow to a luxury real estate market already struggling with uncertainty, as prospective buyers reconsider multimillion-dollar purchases and sellers wait for the market to recover.

Hollywood’s beachfront playground takes another hit

Known simply as the Colony , or the original Malibu, the neighborhood has been a Hollywood power base since the era of Gloria Swanson, Mary Pickford and Charlie Chaplin. Its celebrity connections continued through the decades, with residents including studio mogul Jack Warner, Bing Crosby, Jane Fonda and Frank Capra.

More recent and current residents have included Tom Hanks and Rita Wilson, Ridley Scott, Chris Columbus, Spike Jonze, Jim Carrey, Ed Norton and Red Hot Chili Peppers bassist Flea. The enclave's appeal is easy to understand. Its homes sit close to the Pacific, offering ocean views, direct beach access and a degree of privacy that is difficult to find elsewhere along Southern California's coast. But that proximity to the water has become a growing liability.

The latest waves tore away many oceanfront decks and beach staircases, leaving exposed structures and debris along the shoreline. Although Malibu Colony reportedly escaped some of the more severe flooding experienced in Newport Beach and Long Beach, where waves overtopped seawalls and inundated streets, the damage has left residents bracing for what comes next.

Even a neighborhood accustomed to expensive renovations and elaborate properties is confronting a difficult question: How much uncertainty are buyers willing to accept when a home's greatest selling point is also a source of risk?

Celebrity homes worth millions are struggling to find buyers

The weather has arrived at an especially difficult time for the Colony's luxury property market. Some sellers are holding firm on asking prices, while potential buyers are waiting to see how the coastline fares through the coming months. Among the properties on the market is a home owned by Oscar-winning filmmaker Spike Jonze, known for directing Being John Malkovich, Adaptation, Where the Wild Things Are and Her.

Jonze purchased the five-bedroom Cape Cod-style house for $18 million in 2023. The property, built in 1963, is now listed for $22 million. Its features include ocean views, a swimming pool, a rarity in the Colony, and a main suite with a fireplace, sitting areas, a sundeck and a skylight. A third-floor space could serve as a screening lounge, home office or additional sleeping area, while beamed ceilings and indoor-outdoor entertaining spaces add to its appeal.

Yet even an attractive property with a famous owner is not immune to concerns about coastal flooding. One prospective buyer told the New York Post's Gimme Shelter column that the recent weather had changed their plans. The home's listing broker, Damon Skelton of Compass, declined to comment.

Flea, whose real name is Michael Peter Balzary, is also trying to sell his Colony property. The Red Hot Chili Peppers bassist has reduced the asking price of his four-bedroom home to $7.995 million from $8.495 million in March. Flea purchased the house, built in 1959, for $7.55 million in 2020. Listing brokers Sandro Dazzan and Irene Dazzan-Palmer of The Agency declined to comment.

Wildfires have already devastated Malibu

The coastal damage comes on top of another disaster that has reshaped the community: the wildfires that swept through the region in 2025. Roughly 700 homes within Malibu city limits were destroyed in the Palisades Fire, leaving residents to navigate rebuilding, insurance complications and the loss of homes and neighborhoods.

Malibu is frequently described as North America's wildfire capital, a reputation reinforced by the combination of dry vegetation, steep terrain and powerful Santa Ana winds. On Thursday afternoon, the threat returned when the Bryson Fire broke out in brush near Encinal Canyon Road and Mulholland Highway . Fanned by strong winds, the fire had burned approximately 200 acres by that evening, with no containment reported at the time.

Evacuation orders and warnings were issued for parts of the area, although no structures had burned and no injuries had been reported at the time of the account. For some Colony resident s, the sequence of disasters has created a sense that the community cannot catch a break.

One resident complained that Malibu often receives less sympathy than other fire-affected areas because of its wealth, even though many local homeowners also lost their properties. The comment captures a difficult tension surrounding Malibu's recovery: its residents include some of the wealthiest people in the entertainment industry, but the destruction of homes and the threat of repeated natural disasters affect the community regardless of property values.

Its celebrity connections continued through the decades, with residents including studio mogul Jack Warner, Bing Crosby, Jane Fonda and Frank Capra.

More recent and current residents have included Tom Hanks and Rita Wilson, Ridley Scott, Chris Columbus, Spike Jonze, Jim Carrey, Ed Norton and Red Hot Chili Peppers bassist Flea. The enclave's appeal is easy to understand. Its homes sit close to the Pacific, offering ocean views, direct beach access and a degree of privacy that is difficult to find elsewhere along Southern California's coast. But that proximity to the water has become a growing liability.

The latest waves tore away many oceanfront decks and beach staircases, leaving exposed structures and debris along the shoreline. Although Malibu Colony reportedly escaped some of the more severe flooding experienced in Newport Beach and Long Beach, where waves overtopped seawalls and inundated streets, the damage has left residents bracing for what comes next.

Even a neighborhood accustomed to expensive renovations and elaborate properties is confronting a difficult question: How much uncertainty are buyers willing to accept when a home's greatest selling point is also a source of risk?
Celebrity homes worth millions are struggling to find buyers

The weather has arrived at an especially difficult time for the Colony's luxury property market. Some sellers are holding firm on asking prices, while potential buyers are waiting to see how the coastline fares through the coming months. Among the properties on the market is a home owned by Oscar-winning filmmaker Spike Jonze, known for directing Being John Malkovich, Adaptation, Where the Wild Things Are and Her.

Jonze purchased the five-bedroom Cape Cod-style house for $18 million in 2023. The property, built in 1963, is now listed for $22 million. Its features include ocean views, a swimming pool, a rarity in the Colony, and a main suite with a fireplace, sitting areas, a sundeck and a skylight. A third-floor space could serve as a screening lounge, home office or additional sleeping area, while beamed ceilings and indoor-outdoor entertaining spaces add to its appeal.

Yet even an attractive property with a famous owner is not immune to concerns about coastal flooding. One prospective buyer told the New York Post's Gimme Shelter column that the recent weather had changed their plans. The home's listing broker, Damon Skelton of Compass, declined to comment.

Flea, whose real name is Michael Peter Balzary, is also trying to sell his Colony property. The Red Hot Chili Peppers bassist has reduced the asking price of his four-bedroom home to $7.995 million from $8.495 million in March. Flea purchased the house, built in 1959, for $7.55 million in 2020. Listing brokers Sandro Dazzan and Irene Dazzan-Palmer of The Agency declined to comment.
Wildfires have already devastated Malibu

The coastal damage comes on top of another disaster that has reshaped the community: the wildfires that swept through the region in 2025. Roughly 700 homes within Malibu city limits were destroyed in the Palisades Fire, leaving residents to navigate rebuilding, insurance complications and the loss of homes and neighborhoods.

Malibu is frequently described as North America's wildfire capital, a reputation reinforced by the combination of dry vegetation, steep terrain and powerful Santa Ana winds. On Thursday afternoon, the threat returned when the Bryson Fire broke out in brush near Encinal Canyon Road and Mulholland Highway . Fanned by strong winds, the fire had burned approximately 200 acres by that evening, with no containment reported at the time.

Evacuation orders and warnings were issued for parts of the area, although no structures had burned and no injuries had been reported at the time of the account. For some Colony resident s, the sequence of disasters has created a sense that the community cannot catch a break.

One resident complained that Malibu often receives less sympathy than other fire-affected areas because of its wealth, even though many local homeowners also lost their properties. The comment captures a difficult tension surrounding Malibu's recovery: its residents include some of the wealthiest people in the entertainment industry, but the destruction of homes and the threat of repeated natural disasters affect the community regardless of property values.

articles.title: Alfred Marshall, economist: "The price of a good is the result of the interaction between supply and demand"
articles.standfirst: The British economist laid the foundations for one of the market’s fundamental theories, identified by experts as the main housing problem
articles.summary: The British economist laid the foundations for one of the market’s fundamental theories, identified by experts as the main housing problem
articles.body:
S ome products rise in price while others become cheaper . The answer lies, to a large extent, in the relationship between supply and demand, two essential concepts for understanding how the economy works. The British economist Alfred Marshall (1842-1924) was one of the figures who contributed most to developing this theory, which continues to be used to explain how prices are formed in markets.

Marshall argued that the price of a product does not depend solely on what it costs to produce it or on consumers' interest in buying it. It is the result of the interaction between those who offer a good and those who wish to acquire it. This idea was set out in his work ‘Principles of Economics ’ , published in 1890 , and became a reference for the development of modern microeconomics.

Supply and demand, the two forces that determine prices

Supply represents the quantity of a product that sellers are willing to place on the market at different prices . Demand, for its part, reflects how much consumers want and are able to buy. When both forces coincide, an equilibrium price is reached, at which the quantity supplied corresponds to the quantity demanded.

“The price of a good is the result of the interaction between supply and demand” . With this idea, Alfred Marshall explains that the price of a product depends on the balance between what sellers offer and what consumers are willing to buy.

When a good is in high demand and scarce, its price tends to rise ; conversely, if there are more products available than consumers want to buy, its price usually falls. For example, if many people want to buy a product and only a few units remain, sellers can raise its price. On the other hand, if there are too many units and few buyers, they will have to lower the price to sell them. Thus, the interaction between supply and demand helps determine the price a product reaches in the market.

The economist also studied how the passage of time influences markets. In the short term, production capacity may be limited, while in the long term, companies can invest, expand their facilities, and adapt their supply to buyers' needs.

His legacy continues to be present in current economic analysis. Understanding the relationship between supply and demand makes it possible to interpret everything from variations in food prices to housing costs or changes in certain industrial sectors. A theory that, more than a century later, remains fundamental to explain why we pay more or less for the same product.

articles.title: More than 1.6 million tons of sand dumped in the US to hold back the sea, restore beaches and protect homes and roads
articles.standfirst: The project comes with a $72 million price tag
articles.summary: The project comes with a $72 million price tag
articles.body:
Sometimes, people are forced to confront the sheer power of nature. Along the South Carolina coast, the relentless advance of the sea has pushed local authorities to find ways to hold back the water, restore beaches and, above all, protect homes, roads and other infrastructure increasingly threatened by the encroaching ocean.

The $72 million project will cover roughly 45 kilometers of coastline, including North Myrtle Beach, Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach and Garden City. These areas suffered extensive damage and significant sand loss following Hurricanes Ian in 2022 and Debby in 2024, accelerating the sea’s advance along the coast.

How authorities expanded the beaches to hold back the sea

To protect homes, businesses and roads, authorities used specialized machinery to pump sand from the seabed directly onto the shore through large pipes. Once the sand reached the coast, excavators spread it across the beaches.

In total, 2.15 million cubic yards of sand were used from late 2025 through August 2026, when the project was completed. The new protective barrier not only helps restore the beaches to their former appearance, but also provides protection against future storms and helps reduce the impact of waves.

Today, homes, roads and businesses in the area are better protected, allowing normal activity to resume without the constant concern of the encroaching sea. The water had been getting increasingly close as the natural sand barrier gradually disappeared.

articles.title: Are you getting your Social Security Disability Benefits this Wednesday? Payment schedule for October 2026
articles.standfirst: The next round of benefits is approaching, while an unusual October calendar change means some SSI recipients will receive two deposits
articles.summary: The next round of benefits is approaching, while an unusual October calendar change means some SSI recipients will receive two deposits
articles.body:
Americans waiting for their next Social Security Disability payment could see money arrive in their accounts this Wednesday, although the timing depends largely on their date of birth and when they began receiving benefits.

The Social Security Administration (SSA) will issue its next scheduled round of payments on October 21, continuing a staggered distribution system used for retirement, disability and survivor benefits.

Wednesday's deposits are intended for eligible beneficiaries whose birthdays fall between the 11th and 20th of any month.

Others may have already received their October payment or could be waiting until October 28, while recipients covered by special scheduling rules follow a different timetable.

Who will receive Social Security Disability benefits on October 21?

Most people receiving Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) who began collecting benefits after April 1997 are paid according to their birthday.

Those born between the 1st and 10th generally receive payments on the second Wednesday, while birthdays between the 11th and 20th correspond to the third Wednesday.

Recipients born between the 21st and 31st usually receive their payments on the fourth Wednesday.

The remaining October 2026 schedule is:

October 21: Birthdays from the 11th through the 20th

October 28: Birthdays from the 21st through the 31st

October 30: Early November SSI payment

Beneficiaries who started receiving Social Security before May 1997, along with certain other recipients, were scheduled to receive their October payments on October 2.

Why some Social Security recipients get two October payments

Another important calendar adjustment affects Americans receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI), a separate program supporting eligible people with limited income and resources.

SSI is normally distributed on the first day of each month, but payments are moved forward when that date falls on a weekend or federal holiday.

Because November 1, 2026, falls on a Sunday, the SSA has scheduled November's SSI payment for Friday, October 30.

That means SSI recipients will receive two deposits during October, following their regular payment on October 1.

However, this doesn't represent an increase in benefits or an additional payment. It is simply November's money arriving early.

What happens if Social Security Disability payment is late?

Beneficiaries expecting payment Wednesday should ordinarily receive their money electronically through direct deposit or a Direct Express debit card.

If the payment doesn't appear, the SSA recommends contacting the bank or financial institution first to determine whether a processing delay has occurred.

Recipients who remain unable to locate their benefits can contact Social Security at 1-800-772-1213 or visit their local SSA office.

"We will review the case and if the payment is due, we will replace it," the administration explains in its guidance on missing payments.

Beneficiaries can also check their scheduled payment date through their personal my Social Security account.

With October 21 approaching, checking the correct payment category can help recipients determine whether their money is expected Wednesday or later in the month.

articles.title: NASA cracks the mystery of asteroid Bennu: Its giant rocks reveal a surprising feature
articles.standfirst: The samples collected reveal that the rocks are riddled with numerous internal cracks
articles.summary: The samples collected reveal that the rocks are riddled with numerous internal cracks
articles.body:
Asteroid Bennu has puzzled scientists for years. Its surface is covered with massive boulders, a landscape that should, in principle, retain heat for longer. However, observations from space showed that the asteroid heated up and cooled down unexpectedly quickly. Now, researchers have found an explanation by analyzing samples collected by NASA.

The study, published in Nature Communications, found that Bennu’s rocks contain extensive networks of internal fractures. These cracks, combined with the material’s high porosity, help explain its unusual thermal behavior and solve a mystery that had puzzled researchers for years.

The hidden cracks changing what we know about Bennu

OSIRIS-REx arrived at Bennu in 2018 and encountered a surface far more rugged than expected. Scientists had anticipated large areas covered with fine material, but instead found terrain dominated by large boulders. The mystery deepened when that landscape was compared with previous thermal measurements showing that the asteroid lost heat rapidly.

To investigate the phenomenon, researchers analyzed rock fragments brought back to Earth and used X-ray computed tomography (XCT). The technology allowed them to examine the samples’ internal structure in three dimensions without damaging them. The researchers then used the data in computer simulations to study how heat moves through larger rocks.

The results showed that porosity alone was not enough to explain the phenomenon. The internal fractures were a crucial piece of the puzzle. “They’re really cracked up, and that was the missing piece,” explained Andrew Ryan, a researcher at the University of Arizona who led the team responsible for analyzing the samples’ physical and thermal properties.

The discovery could also help scientists better interpret observations of other asteroids. Until now, researchers have faced challenges connecting thermal measurements made from space with the actual physical properties of asteroid rocks. Directly analyzing extraterrestrial material provides a way to connect the two types of data and improve our understanding of these celestial bodies.

articles.title: Which Costco will you find the Russet House sweet potato fries in and how much they cost?
articles.standfirst: Russet House's popular frozen fries have appeared at warehouses nationwide, but stock and prices vary by location
articles.summary: Russet House's popular frozen fries have appeared at warehouses nationwide, but stock and prices vary by location
articles.body:
A frozen side dish is attracting unexpected attention at Costco , where shoppers have been praising Russet House Organic Sweet Potato Fries as an easy addition to their weekly grocery lists.

The Canadian-made product recently topped Tasting Table's ranking of six seasonal Costco foods, beating several more elaborate offerings thanks to its natural flavor and ability to become crispy in an air fryer.

Unlike products designed specifically for Halloween or the holiday season, the fries offer an everyday alternative that can accompany burgers, chicken or other main dishes throughout the year.

However, shoppers hoping to purchase the popular four-pound bag may need to check their nearest warehouse before making the trip.

Which Costco locations stock Russet House sweet potato fries?

Russet House Organic Sweet Potato Fries are sold in Costco's frozen food section under item number 2013953, although distribution and stock levels differ between locations.

Warehouse inventory trackers have recorded the product at stores in California, Texas, North Carolina, South Carolina and Georgia.

Among the locations previously reporting availability are Culver City and Lancaster in California, Wilmington in North Carolina, and Kyle in Texas.

Atlanta-area Costco warehouses have also carried the fries, including locations around Cumberland Mall, Perimeter and Stone Mountain.

These listings establish where the product has been sold, rather than guaranteeing that every warehouse currently has bags available.

Costco advises customers to select their preferred store through its website or app to check inventory information where that feature is available.

How much do Russet House sweet potato fries cost?

The four-pound bags have recently been listed at warehouse prices ranging from $8.99 to $9.99, depending on location.

Customers ordering through Costco 's same-day delivery service may pay more, with the retailer displaying a price of $10.77 for the same four-pound package.

The lower in-store prices work out to roughly $2.25 to $2.50 per pound, making the fries an appealing bulk purchase for families.

The product's popularity comes largely from its convenience and the crisp texture achieved during cooking.

The fries have been praised for retaining their naturally sweet, earthy flavor while developing a crunchy exterior in less than 20 minutes.

The recipe uses a coating of rice flour and cornstarch, while the US version contains olive or avocado oil rather than seed oils.

The fries are also marketed as organic, vegan and free from added sugar, offering shoppers several options for incorporating them into everyday meals.

One TikTok customer described the product enthusiastically, saying: "I've been having these almost every single day... These are better than restaurant sweet potato fries."

Their popularity makes them worth considering during a Costco visit, particularly for shoppers looking for convenient freezer staples.

articles.title: Abraham Lincoln, U.S. President: ”Always bear in mind that your own resolution to succeed is more important than any other one thing"
articles.standfirst: Lincoln once shared a powerful lesson about determination with a young man hoping to become a lawyer
articles.summary: Lincoln once shared a powerful lesson about determination with a young man hoping to become a lawyer
articles.body:
Long before Abraham Lincoln entered the White House, he faced a question familiar to anyone hoping to build a career without the advantages of wealth, connections or an established professional network.

How could someone pursue an ambitious goal when the conventional path appeared inaccessible? In November 1855, the future president addressed that dilemma in a letter to Isham Reavis , a young man seeking advice about becoming a lawyer.

Lincoln couldn't offer Reavis a place studying alongside him, explaining that his demanding schedule made it difficult to provide the necessary supervision. Instead, he encouraged the young man to take responsibility for his education.

"If you are resolutely determined to make a lawyer of yourself, the thing is more than half done already," Lincoln wrote.

His letter concluded with a statement that would become one of his most frequently repeated observations about success.

Lincoln 's advice was rooted in personal experience rather than abstract philosophy.

Born in Kentucky in 1809, he grew up with limited access to formal education and never attended college or law school.

His entry into the legal profession came through independent reading, an approach that required considerable discipline at a time when aspiring lawyers commonly studied under experienced attorneys.

Lincoln explained to Reavis that the absence of a mentor or prestigious educational institution did not necessarily prevent someone from acquiring professional knowledge.

"I did not read with any one," he wrote. "Get the books, and read and study them till, you understand them in their principal features; and that is the main thing."

The message wasn't that education lacked importance. Lincoln was emphasizing that learning could take place outside established institutions when someone possessed the resources and determination to pursue it.

A consistent philosophy about hard work

The 1855 correspondence was not an isolated example of Lincoln offering practical advice to aspiring lawyers.

Three years later, he encouraged William H. Grigsby to study independently rather than become preoccupied with where he lived or whom he could study under.

His guidance was similarly direct in September 1860, when John M. Brockman requested advice about developing a comprehensive understanding of the law.

"The mode is very simple, though laborious, and tedious," Lincoln explained, recommending careful study of established legal texts. "Work, work, work, is the main thing."

Together, the letters reveal Lincoln 's consistent belief that meaningful progress depended on sustained effort rather than shortcuts or favorable circumstances alone.

Why Abraham Lincoln's advice remains relevant today

Lincoln eventually became the 16th president of the United States, leading the country through the Civil War and helping bring about the abolition of slavery.

His achievements cannot be explained solely through personal determination, and his advice does not mean that economic hardship or unequal access to opportunities are insignificant.

Nevertheless, the principle behind his words remains relevant to people pursuing education, professional advancement or difficult personal ambitions.

Lincoln 's central argument was that circumstances shouldn't automatically determine whether someone attempts to achieve a goal.

His advice to Reavis recognized something fundamental about progress: external support can make success easier, but individual commitment influences whether available opportunities are used.

More than 170 years later, the letter remains a reminder that determination is not a guarantee of achievement, but it can be the foundation on which achievement becomes possible.

articles.standfirst: The granddaughter of Robert F. Kennedy and Ethel Kennedy dedicated her career to education and disability rights before her death
articles.summary: The granddaughter of Robert F. Kennedy and Ethel Kennedy dedicated her career to education and disability rights before her death
articles.body:
Kyle Kennedy , granddaughter of Robert F. Kennedy and Ethel Kennedy , has died at 42, according to her obituary.

She passed away at her home in Westwood, Massachusetts, on September 21. Officials haven't confirmed a cause of death, and the circumstances remain under investigation.

articles.title: The fattest “squid” in history is found in Wyoming: it lived 160 million years ago and its fossil spent decades forgotten in a drawer
articles.standfirst: Scientists from the United States, the United Kingdom, and New Zealand share their advances
articles.summary: Scientists from the United States, the United Kingdom, and New Zealand share their advances
articles.body:
Dr. Dean Lomax , honorary researcher at the University of Manchester, has led a research team made up of scientists from the United States, the United Kingdom, and New Zealand . This group of experts, as they explain in the journal Papers in Paleontology, has discovered in Wyoming the fattest squid ever known, which lived some 160 million years ago.

This is a ‘Wyoteuthis linsterorum’, known as a belemnite , which is an extinct prehistoric species that was related to present-day squid and octopuses. It stood out for having a very thick, barrel-shaped internal structure . In the case of the latter identified, it is the largest ever found to date.

The incredible dimensions of this squid

Typically, according to data from the Sundance Formation in Wyoming, the fossils are between five and 10 centimeters long, and between one and two centimeters wide . Its face is about 10 centimeters long and six centimeters wide. It is believed that when they were alive they reached about 60 centimeters.

This group of experts used a technique known as computed tomography (CT) and analyzed the internal structures of the fossils. In doing so, they realized that there was a connection to a family of belemnites believed to have gone extinct long before this type of animal lived.

“One possible explanation is that their relatively large size gave them an advantage when hunting smaller belemnites of the genus Pachyteuthis that coexisted in the same habitat. After all, modern squids are not at all picky when it comes to choosing their prey: they readily hunt not only other species of cephalopods , but sometimes even those of their own species,” says Alexey Ippolitov, a belemnite expert and member of Victoria University of Wellington.

articles.title: Who is Stephen Hubbard? Retired American teacher freed by Russia after Trump intervenes
articles.standfirst: He was sentenced after a closed trial in 2024 to nearly seven years in prison
articles.summary: He was sentenced after a closed trial in 2024 to nearly seven years in prison
articles.body:
Russia on Wednesday released a retired American teacher who had been imprisoned on charges of fighting as a mercenary in Ukraine, U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff said Wednesday at a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg.

The release of Stephen Hubbard had been foreshadowed a day earlier in Washington, when President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House that he had talked with Putin “at length” about the issue and had asked him to free the Michigan man.

Hubbard is the second American detainee in just over two months to be freed by Russia, and his exit from custody occurred not only during a visit by Witkoff but also at a time when Trump has taken a series of actions meant to benefit Russia as Washington's alliance with Ukraine shows signs of fraying.

Hubbard was sentenced after a closed trial in 2024 to nearly seven years in prison. Prosecutors said he had signed a contract with the Ukrainian military after Russia sent troops into Ukraine in February 2022, and that he fought alongside them until being captured two months later. The U.S. government under the Biden administration designated Hubbard as wrongfully detained.

Witkoff, a key Trump administration envoy who has tried without success to steer Russia and Ukraine toward a settlement to end a war that will hit the five-year mark in February, thanked Putin for releasing Hubbard, telling him, “Because of you, he's going home to his family.” The Russian leader responded that Hubbard was at the St. Petersburg airport, Pulkovo, after the release.

The release occurred at a dynamic moment in relations between the United States, Ukraine and Russia, with the Washington-Kyiv alliance being stretched by tensions over drone support as the Trump administration advances policies that aid Putin.

Trump decided Friday, for instance, to waive sanctions on Russia in a bill that Congress overwhelmingly passed to support Ukraine. Named after late South Carolina Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham, the legislation targeted the flow of financial resources fueling Russia’s war.

That reversal followed Trump’s announcement of a deal to import Russian diesel fuel in a long-shot effort to curb high gas prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections next month.

Witkoff met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Norway on Tuesday. He was expected to exchange ideas from that meeting, as well as proposals from European and American colleagues, in his talks with Russian leaders in St. Petersburg on Wednesday.

Hubbard is the second American freed by Russia in about the last two months, following the release in August of Marine veteran Robert Gilman, who had been gravely ill and was imprisoned on disputed charges of assaulting a police officer.

Some two dozen Americans remain imprisoned in Russia for various reasons, according to the Foley Foundation, a hostage advocacy organization.

Hubbard had been imprisoned since 2022 on charges that Hostage Aid Worldwide, a hostage advocacy group, has called bogus.

The organization in August posted an open letter to Trump that it said was written by Patricia Hubbard Fox, Hubbard’s sister, in which she offered praise for Trump but also said brother had been subjected to “constant beatings, torture and starvation” while in custody.

“Even so, everything that you’re doing isn’t going to matter to my kidnapped, American Veteran brother, Stephen James Hubbard (soon to be 74) if Putin won’t cave and let him come home and he dies up there in a Nazi prison (crying),” the letter said.

articles.title: Retirement income vs wage growth: What are the differences that you must consider and the latest changes for 2027?
articles.standfirst: The 2027 Cost-of-Living Adjustment has been set at 3.6% but what does it mean?
articles.summary: The 2027 Cost-of-Living Adjustment has been set at 3.6% but what does it mean?
articles.body:
Retirees and workers face different rules for income growth in 2027, with Social Security benefits set to rise by 3.6% while wage growth for employees who remain in their jobs has been slower as the difference highlights how inflation and labor market conditions affect household finances. The Social Security Administration (SSA) announced the 2027 Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) for approximately 72 million beneficiaries, with payments scheduled to increase in January.

Meanwhile, the September three-month moving average for year-over-year median wage growth among job stayers stood at 3.4%, below the benefit adjustment and the Social Security 's annual COLA is designed to help benefits keep pace with inflation, using a measure of consumer prices during the third quarter. Wage growth, by contrast, reflects what employers pay workers and can depend on labor demand, skills, industry conditions and whether someone changes jobs thus retirees are believed to have received larger increases than job stayers in three of the past six years. For example, one notable example was the 8.7% COLA announced in 2022 for 2023, when inflation surged following the COVID-19 pandemic meaning inflation remains a key consideration. The consumer price index rose 3.7% year over year in September, above the Federal Reserve 's 2% target. Although inflation has eased from its 2022 highs, higher living costs continue to shape both retirees' budgets and workers' demands for better pay.

Could job switching deliver stronger income growth in 2027?

Workers who change employers have recently experienced stronger wage growth than those who stay in their positions as the latest figures put job switchers ahead of both job stayers and the 3.6% Social Security adjustment, although individual outcomes vary. Changing jobs is not necessarily an easy route to higher earnings, and hiring has remained subdued in the United States , with relatively low layoffs but limited job openings. Some white-collar industries have recorded employment losses, while leisure and hospitality employment has been volatile. That low-hire, low-fire environment can provide some security for people who already have jobs - but it may also weaken their leverage when negotiating raises as some employees have responded by making their achievements more visible to managers and professional networks. Alongside the 2027 COLA , the SSA has reported a major effort to improve the accuracy of Social Security number records as the agency said it had corrected nearly 50 million records since January 2025. That figure includes some 17 million missing dates of death and approximately 25 million records with missing citizenship information whilst the SSA is also working to correct another 8.5 million records containing inaccurate citizenship details. Commissioner Frank J. Bisignano said accurate records help prevent fraud and support the proper administration of government services. For beneficiaries, the cleanup does not mean Social Security numbers are being taken away, or monthly payments are automatically changing.

articles.standfirst: No winning ticket was found on Monday, October 19 meaning the jackpot prize rolls over
articles.summary: No winning ticket was found on Monday, October 19 meaning the jackpot prize rolls over
articles.body:
The Powerball jackpot has risen to an estimated $635 million for Wednesday, October 21, after no ticket matched all six numbers in Monday's drawing as the prize carries an estimated cash value of $635 million for a winner choosing the lump sum.

The jackpot has been growing since a player in Illinois won $1.04 billion in August. Wednesday's drawing gives players another chance to claim the prize, although the winning numbers and jackpot outcome are not yet published.

The drawing for the winning numbers for Wednesday, October 21, is scheduled for around 22:59 ET/17:00 PT, and players can watch it live through the official Powerball website for the latest outcome.

Monday's drawing on October 19 produced the numbers 8, 31, 32, 42 and 48, with Powerball 23. The Power Play multiplier was 4X, but no ticket matched all five white balls and the red Powerball to take the jackpot in that drawing.

That means no player won the jackpot or the $2 million Match 5 + Power Play prize– although one ticket holder in Michigan did win $1 million by matching the five white-ball numbers.

As the jackpot was not won on October 19, so it rolled over and reached an estimated $635 million for Wednesday. The advertised prize is paired with a cash value of $267.5 million, before any applicable taxes are taken into account at both state and federal level.

How to play Powerball with the chance to win $635 million

Tickets cost $2 per play and are sold in 45 states, Washington, D.C. , Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands and depending on local laws, players may also be able to buy tickets online when visiting a participating jurisdiction.

To play, choose five white-ball numbers from 1 to 69 and one red Powerball number from 1 to 26. Players can select their own combination or use Quick Pick to have a computer generate the numbers for them.

Power Play costs an additional $1 and can multiply non-jackpot prizes by 2X, 3X, 4X, 5X or 10X. The jackpot requires a ticket to match all five white balls and the red Powerball , rather than relying on the multiplier alone.

The odds of winning the jackpot are 1 in 292.2 million and those odds remain the same for players across the United States and in the United Kingdom , as British citizens are also eligible to compete in Powerball .

Power Play can change eligible non-jackpot payouts rather than improve the chance of winning the top prize and players can check the official results after the scheduled drawing for the outcome.

articles.title: Katie Zacharia gets back to her routine in California after abrupt five-day stint as Trump’s press secretary
articles.standfirst: The former conservative commentator was spotted out for a walk days after her rocky White House debut and sudden departure
articles.summary: The former conservative commentator was spotted out for a walk days after her rocky White House debut and sudden departure
articles.body:
K atie Zacharia is back in California, and her first public appearance since leaving the White House came with a bold red, white and blue workout look . Photos published by TMZ show the former press secretary walking through her neighborhood in a blue sports bra, red leggings, white socks and sneakers, with her blonde hair pulled into a side braid. The sighting came just days after her five-day run in one of Washington’s most visible jobs came to an abrupt end.

Zacharia’s route to the podium ran through conservative media. She appeared regularly on Fox News and Newsmax, worked as a communications adviser for Trump Media and Truth Social, and briefly served as a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security. She had also interned at the White House during George W. Bush’s presidency. Her connection to Donald Trump was largely through that media orbit : Zacharia said she made sure to appear on television discussing issues she knew he followed, figuring that if he saw her and liked her, he might recruit her.

Trump announced her appointment on Oct. 9, calling her a loyal supporter, and she started the job on Oct. 12. The pick surprised people inside the White House; according to The Washington Post, Trump made the decision without first consulting some senior aides. Zacharia had replaced Karoline Leavitt, who had worked with Trump for years and had a much closer relationship with him.

One briefing, mounting questions and a fast exit

Her first and only briefing lasted about 14 minutes. Zacharia appeared nervous as she read from a prepared script, took questions from three reporters and struggled to answer one about Ukraine. She also mistakenly referred to her husband as the president.

The appearance drew criticism, but questions about her legal credentials soon became a bigger problem: although she had a law degree from Pepperdine, she acknowledged that she had never passed a bar exam. Trump had called her an attorney when he announced her appointment.

The scrutiny followed her into television interviews. Sean Hannity pressed her about her qualifications, and she faced more questions about her background on Fox & Friends. On Oct. 16, Trump told reporters she should reconsider the job, saying he wanted her to be happy and did not think she needed to face the media’s criticism.

Her departure was confirmed shortly afterward. Trump described it as her decision; reports said she was leaving the role after five days.

Her short tenure also sparked attention around her look and polished, feminine style, which some fashion coverage compared with the aesthetic associated with Melania Trump.

But there’s no reliable report confirming that the first lady disliked Zacharia or her appearance . For now, Zacharia’s California walk gives the story a quieter postscript: after a turbulent week at the White House, she has returned to her own routine. The difference now is that she’s famous and widely known, though perhaps not in the way she wanted.

articles.title: President Donald Trump wants the press out of White House to make room for new indoor pool
articles.standfirst: The administration has declined to rule out moving reporters as plans to revive Roosevelt's former swimming pool resurface
articles.summary: The administration has declined to rule out moving reporters as plans to revive Roosevelt's former swimming pool resurface
articles.body:
The room where American presidents and their spokespeople have faced questions from journalists for decades could soon serve a very different purpose, with President Donald Trump reportedly revisiting plans to transform it into an indoor swimming pool.

The president has repeatedly discussed moving reporters out of the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room , according to The New York Times, which cited three people familiar with conversations inside the administration.

Trump reportedly raised the proposal several times with former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt , including during the final weeks before her departure on August 27.

He even suggested that removing the journalists could become her "last legacy," although the proposal was not implemented before she left office.

The idea remains under consideration, with the White House declining to announce whether any renovation or relocation will proceed.

The proposal has an unusual historical connection because the current briefing room occupies the site of a swimming pool installed during Franklin D. Roosevelt 's presidency.

Built in 1933, the pool allowed Roosevelt to exercise in water as part of managing the effects of polio, which had left him with significant mobility limitations.

It remained part of the White House for decades until President Richard Nixon had it covered in 1970, creating space for the growing presidential press corps.

Trump has reportedly expressed interest in reversing that transformation, even sharing contrasting images on Truth Social in September.

One depicted the existing briefing room beneath the words "Fake News," while another showed a proposed swimming pool labeled "FDR Pool."

White House journalists could lose West Wing workspace

Restoring the pool would require relocating journalists who currently work close to the Oval Office and senior administration officials.

One option reportedly involves transferring them to the Eisenhower Executive Office Building , which stands immediately beside the White House complex.

Former Trump strategist Steve Bannon has supported moving reporters away from the West Wing, citing concerns about security.

"From the moment I arrived in the White House, I believed it was a national security threat to have the press literally surround the Oval Office," Bannon told The New York Times.

Journalists, however, have raised broader concerns about restrictions on their proximity to officials and opportunities to ask questions directly.

A relocation could preserve formal briefings while changing the informal access reporters have traditionally enjoyed.

Trump faces questions over press access

The discussions come amid an ongoing legal dispute involving CNN, Politico and MS NOW over restrictions on their White House coverage.

A federal judge recently granted preliminary relief to the news organizations, although CNN has alleged that access problems continue, including restrictions involving Air Force One.

White House communications director Steven Cheung defended the administration's position toward the media while leaving the proposed changes unresolved.

"America is rightly distrustful of the fake news media because they fabricate stories based off lies and sources who are not even privy to any type of information," Cheung said.

articles.title: Costco Kirkland Châteauneuf-du-Pape Winemaker: Who Makes It, and What Are Other Options You Can Find?
articles.standfirst: Costco's Rhône Valley red comes from a respected French winemaker, offering shoppers an affordable way to explore a famous wine region
articles.summary: Costco's Rhône Valley red comes from a respected French winemaker, offering shoppers an affordable way to explore a famous wine region
articles.body:
C ostco 's Kirkland Signature wines have built a following among shoppers looking for bottles that deliver more than their price tags suggest.

One of the standout options is the retailer's Châteauneuf-du-Pape, a French red wine that normally commands a premium because of its prestigious appellation and long winemaking tradition.

But who actually makes the bottle carrying Costco's name? The answer is Guillaume Gonnet , a third-generation winemaker based in France's southern Rhône Valley.

Rather than relying on an anonymous bulk producer, Costco works with a winemaker who also sells wines under his own name. The partnership helps explain why the Kirkland version has attracted attention from wine enthusiasts looking for value.

The wine is typically priced around $20 to $25 in the United States, although the exact cost can vary by vintage, location and availability. That's considerably less than many bottles from the same appellation, where established producers often charge substantially more.

According to Costco UK's product information, the 2022 Kirkland Signature Châteauneuf-du-Pape was created by Gonnet and brings together fruit from the appellation's different terroirs.

The retailer describes a deep-purple wine with blackberry and cassis notes, complemented by cedar and concentrated fruit flavours. It recommends pairing the bottle with lamb, pork or poultry.

For shoppers, the attraction is straightforward: access to a recognised French wine style without paying the price usually associated with a prestigious regional label.

Why Guillaume Gonnet is behind Costco's French red

Gonnet belongs to a winemaking family with deep roots in the Rhône Valley. His experience in Châteauneuf-du-Pape gives the Kirkland label a direct connection to the region rather than simply borrowing its name.

The wine is a blend led by Grenache, with Syrah, Cinsault and Mourvèdre completing the mix. The commonly reported composition is 70% Grenache and 10% of each of the other three varieties.

Each grape contributes something different. Grenache supplies ripe fruit and body, Syrah can add darker flavours and spice, Mourvèdre contributes structure, and Cinsault helps bring aromatic freshness. Together, they create the kind of layered red blend associated with the southern Rhône.

Châteauneuf-du-Pape itself is among France's best-known wine appellations. Its vineyards feature a mixture of pebbles, clay, sand and limestone, while the warm Mediterranean climate helps grapes ripen fully.

The region's distinctive rounded stones can absorb heat during the day and release it after sunset, contributing to the conditions in which the vines grow.

The name also carries centuries of history, with the area closely associated with the papacy in Avignon during the 14th century. Its reputation today rests on a combination of place, grape varieties and winemaking tradition, not simply the prestige of its label??.

articles.title: Trump called Google to change the name of the Atlantic and give it his surname: "We’ll call it the Trump Ocean"
articles.standfirst: The president claims that Google's CEO rejected the request
articles.summary: The president claims that Google's CEO rejected the request
articles.body:
After the Gulf of America , Donald Trump has set his sights on a much bigger target. The President told his supporters that he tried to change the name of one of the planet's great oceans , and that the response he received was not what he expected.

During a rally, Trump said that he contacted Google to ask that Google Maps rename the Atlantic Ocean as the “ Trump Ocean ” . According to his version, he spoke with the company's CEO, Sundar Pichai , to whom he directly put forward the proposal.

Google to Trump: “Please, don’t ask us to do that”

But this time the answer was negative . Trump explained that the company told him that the oceans are different because they span many countries. Recounting the response he received, the president summarized it this way: “Please don't ask us to do that.”

The president said he would let the refusal pass and that the Atlantic would continue to be called that. Although he clarified that it was a joke , he also acknowledged that, thinking it over, it seemed to him that “it was not a bad idea.” In addition, he floated other options, such as calling the Pacific the “Trump Ocean” or using the name “Ocean of the Americas” .

From the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America

It is not the first time Trump has pushed for a geographic name change. At the beginning of his second term, he signed an executive order to rename the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America , and on that occasion Google Maps did apply the change for users in the United States.

The president maintains that back then a single phone call was enough for the company to agree, and he even claims they told him it was “a great idea” . He also boasts about the commercial success of the new name, such as the sale of Gulf of America caps.

Google has already explained on other occasions that the geographic names on its platform are based on official sources and that it applies specific policies for places whose names vary between countries.

articles.title: 'The Leaders They Trusted Lied': Over 170,000 Pages of Newly Released Records Expose 9/11 Air Quality Cover-Up
articles.standfirst: Mayor Zohran Mamdani announces more releases in the coming months
articles.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani announces more releases in the coming months
articles.body:
More than two decades later after the attacks on the Twin Towers , New York continues to bring to light what happened in the days that followed. The city has made public thousands of new files on one of the most delicate issues of that tragedy : what those who worked and lived near Ground Zero breathed.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced this Wednesday the release of 40,000 related documents on 9/11 , in addition to the records on air quality at Ground Zero disclosed in September. In total, they exceed 200,000 pages and can be consulted on a portal created by the city.

The release comes after a legal battle lasting several years and puts an end to two lawsuits by the organization 9/11 Health Watch . Mamdani recalled that emergency crews, elected officials, and relatives of victims of illnesses linked to 9/11 had been demanding these documents for years.

The memorandum that warned of toxic air

The portal includes the so-called Harding Memorandum , attributed to Robert Harding , deputy mayor in 2001. It privately warned of the serious risks of exposure to toxic substances , while municipal and federal authorities assured that the air in Lower Manhattan was safe.

It also brings together the 170,000 documents from the so-called Box 68 , which according to those affected show that information about the air’s toxicity was concealed. Benjamin Chevat, executive director of 9/11 Health Watch, said that his review has revealed “a troubling picture” .

More documents in the coming months

Mamdani argued that the survivors and More documents in the coming months cannot be limited to the anniversary of the attacks, and indicated that more files will be published in the coming months.

More documents in the coming months to maintain the portal. City Hall announced staff dedicated to recovering certificates for those who need to prove they were in the exposure zone and apply for help from federal programs.

articles.title: In the United States, they collected 5,000 discarded Christmas trees instead of throwing them into landfills: they sank them in a lake to create a shelter for fish
articles.standfirst: In addition, fishing enthusiasts will be able to benefit from this
articles.summary: In addition, fishing enthusiasts will be able to benefit from this
articles.body:
When Christmas ends, the same question arises in millions of homes across the United States , especially those that use real trees rather than plastic ones: What to do with the tree? While most end up in the trash, in the state of Kentucky they have found a more than curious alternative, but a very effective one for giving them a second life.

The regional government has made the decision to collect them, last year they managed to gather around 5,000 natural fir trees delivered by residents. Instead of incinerating them or piling them up in landfills, the Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources set this plan in motion: to sink 1,700 of these trees into the depths of Lake Boltz.

What is the purpose of sinking Christmas trees in a lake?

The initiative, dubbed Christmas for the Fishes, addresses a serious environmental problem. Most of the region's reservoirs are artificial and were created more than half a century ago. Over the decades, the wood and vegetation on the bottom have rotted away, leaving aquatic species without protection.

By submerging the trees grouped “with ecological counterweights, the branches form an intricate underwater network,” they said in a statement. This acts as a natural shield where smaller fish , such as catfish or perch, can evade predators, feed, and reproduce safely.

The impact is not only for the ecosystem, but also for fishing enthusiasts, who can benefit from it . Fish tend to gather in large numbers around these wooden structures. To facilitate fishing activity in the area, biologists record the exact GPS coordinates of the submerged fir trees and share them in a public mobile app, thus making it easier for anglers who come to the area.

articles.title: Tree falls on US couple's home, but they lose €85,000 insurance claim after rejecting the evidence
articles.standfirst: An accident whose legal outcome ended up being key
articles.summary: An accident whose legal outcome ended up being key
articles.body:
Accidents caused by a natural disaster, whether from a hurricane, storm, tsunami, or any other type of phenomenon, are covered by many home insurance policies. When these types of cases occur, companies usually pay the required amount to those affected or offer them solutions that ease the losses.

On August 27, 2022, a tree fell on the Cains family's house in the United State s. According to the Times of India, the couple had taken out a policy with State Farm , which came to carry out the corresponding report and assess the damage, confirming that the tree had pierced the roof.

In its document, the insurer also included other key sections: it did not include as damage resulting from the tree falling other types of defects , which it linked to long-term problems with the home due to temperatures, maintenance, and the settling of the ground itself.

The errors in the report that ended up being the key to the case

State Farm ended up paying the Cains $10,042.90 , a figure far removed from the engineers' reports and a contractor's estimate to repair the home: $95,896.07 . It was then that the family challenged the valuation and a dispute began, during which State Farm initially added another $3,130.08.

In June 2024, the legal battle began and the family relied on Sean Fee for their report . This expert, however, requested the repairs but did not include a breakdown of the costs. In addition, he made a mistake by including a colleague, Jim Irmiter , also from Forensic Building Science. Since the family had only officially designated Fee , this ended up creating a new problem.

The United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit ultimately dismissed Fee's reports and testimony due to those errors and because it considered it impossible to verify who had carried out the analysis. Despite challenging it again, the Cains were left without the compensation and State Farm avoided paying a much larger settlement.

articles.title: 'A young woman from California comes back from partying and discovers a 50 billion dollar debt in her account: "What do I do now?"'
articles.standfirst: Maddie McGivern's case was very popular on social media
articles.summary: Maddie McGivern's case was very popular on social media
articles.body:
Maddie McGivern , a young woman from California , went out for a drink with her friends. She took out her credit card and paid the bill . So far, everything was normal. Just another weekend in her life. The surprise came when, while heading home, the young woman took her mobile phone out of her bag to check the balance of her bank account . And she discovered a completely surreal figure: she had a debt of $49,999,999,697 .

Owing nearly 50 billion dollars after a night out was not in her plans, so Maddie McGivern , completely bewildered and alarmed, immediately called her bank. After a few moments of tension and confusion, the institution cleared up her doubt: it was a massive technical error. "I swear to God it shows a debt of 49 billion dollars. What do I do now?" , she said in a video posted on social media.

The images clearly show how her bank account has an astronomical negative balance and also indicate that she has $76.28 available. Savings that seem insufficient to deal with a debt more typical of a large company's accounting than the cost of a few drinks in a pub. Her friends cannot hold back their laughter while Maddie McGivern shows her mobile phone to the camera.

Maddie McGivern, a viral story with 14 million views

This episode, which took place in June 2021 , has become a small classic in the little-told history of the Internet, going viral again from time to time across different social media platforms. The video by her friend @gabefloress is still available on TikTok and has amassed more than 14 million views and over two million likes.

The comments reacted with surprise and humor to this situation: "I love how she says 49 billion and doesn't care about the remaining 999,999,697" . Obviously, the bank solved the problem without any additional complications for Maddie McGivern , beyond the initial scare.
