articles.title: The forenses transporter who saved a life: The moment a technician saw a 'dead' baby moving under the morgue sheet
articles.standfirst: Vincent, 18 months old, was declared dead after suffering a suspected drowning in Arizona
articles.summary: Vincent, 18 months old, was declared dead after suffering a suspected drowning in Arizona
articles.body:
Alexus Fiordilino will never forget the moment when she hugged her 18-month-old son, Vincent, to say goodbye to him and thought she heard that he was still breathing. The doctor treating him assured her that these were his final gasps and confirmed his death . However, five hours later, the family received a call that changed everything: the little boy was alive and had been found breathing in the morgue of a hospital in Arizona.

The incident occurred almost nine months ago at Mercy Gilbert Medical Center, in the town of Gilbert, and has caused renewed shock after new details about what happened came to light. In an interview with NBC News , Fiordilino, 30, acknowledged that she still regrets not trusting her instinct when she thought she sensed that her son was still alive . " As a mother, you don’t want to hear that. I didn’t want him to suffer. It seemed like they had done everything possible ," she explained, recalling the words of Dr. Aryan Toosi, who allegedly told her that trying new maneuvers to save the little boy would only prolong his agony.

Vincent suffered an alleged drowning and was treated at the hospital. However, he was pronounced dead at 6:20 p.m. on Super Bowl Sunday. Nevertheless, several testimonies collected in police reports indicate that the child may have continued showing signs of breathing after his death had been certified.

'The officers heard "gasping" after his death'

The case has raised doubts about the actions of the healthcare staff. According to police reports, the officers who were in the emergency department observed that the little boy seemed to still be having difficulty breathing after having been declared dead. One of the police officers said he had heard " an audible gasp ." When he returned approximately an hour later to photograph the body, he stated that he again observed what appeared to be " a gasp or a release of air ."

The nurse, for her part, maintained that it was agonal breathing and explained that it could be related to the compressions, the oxygen, and the possible pressure exerted by the family members as they said goodbye to the child. However, when the medical examiner's team arrived hours later to collect the body, they realized that Vincent was still breathing. By then, around five hours had passed since his death had been certified.

The family then received the news that the little boy was still alive, although he needed hospital care and medical assistance. " My husband and I screamed with relief. We were praising the Lord. We were crying. Going from hearing that he was gone to finding out that he is not gone is an indescribable feeling ," Fiordilino recalled.

The family is preparing a complaint against the doctor and the hospital

Medical conduct is now at the center of the controversy. The mother's lawyer, John Brewer, has announced that he plans to file a formal complaint against Dr. Toosi and the hospital over what happened. " The parents were forced to decide whether they should keep trying to resuscitate their son and the doctor provided them with false information ," stressed the attorney, who believes that what happened constitutes a serious lack of respect for human life.

For his part, the doctor's defense has expressed regret over the situation and wished the child a speedy recovery. " Dr. Toosi extends his sympathies to the young patient and his family, and wishes the child a speedy recovery ," it said in a statement in which he also reaffirmed his commitment to quality medical care. As for the hospital, it described what happened as " heartbreaking ," although it declined to offer details about the care provided to the minor for privacy reasons. " Patient safety and exceptional care are our highest priorities ," it said in a statement. The Prosecutor's Office had not yet made a decision on reviewing the case at the time this information was released.

The little boy suffers a severe brain injury and is recovering at home

The little boy's story has also been surrounded by controversy from the beginning. After the alleged drowning, Gilbert Police recommended filing child abuse charges against the parents, after both admitted they had lost sight of Vincent during a party held for the Super Bowl. According to the police report, they also admitted to having smoked marijuana that morning. Ultimately, Maricopa County Attorney Rachel Mitchell announced that no charges would be filed against Alexus Fiordilino and her husband.

Now, the family's main concern is the boy's health. Vincent suffers from a severe brain injury, cannot swallow, has seizures, and cannot sit up or crawl on his own, according to the information released about his condition. Despite the aftereffects, the little boy has been able to return home, where he continues recovering with his parents. His case has reopened the debate over the circumstances of his declaration of death and the possible responsibilities arising from what happened at the hospital.

Vincent suffered an alleged drowning and was treated at the hospital. However, he was pronounced dead at 6:20 p.m. on Super Bowl Sunday. Nevertheless, several testimonies collected in police reports indicate that the child may have continued showing signs of breathing after his death had been certified.
'The officers heard "gasping" after his death'

The case has raised doubts about the actions of the healthcare staff. According to police reports, the officers who were in the emergency department observed that the little boy seemed to still be having difficulty breathing after having been declared dead. One of the police officers said he had heard " an audible gasp ." When he returned approximately an hour later to photograph the body, he stated that he again observed what appeared to be " a gasp or a release of air ."

The nurse, for her part, maintained that it was agonal breathing and explained that it could be related to the compressions, the oxygen, and the possible pressure exerted by the family members as they said goodbye to the child. However, when the medical examiner's team arrived hours later to collect the body, they realized that Vincent was still breathing. By then, around five hours had passed since his death had been certified.

The family then received the news that the little boy was still alive, although he needed hospital care and medical assistance. " My husband and I screamed with relief. We were praising the Lord. We were crying. Going from hearing that he was gone to finding out that he is not gone is an indescribable feeling ," Fiordilino recalled.
The family is preparing a complaint against the doctor and the hospital

Medical conduct is now at the center of the controversy. The mother's lawyer, John Brewer, has announced that he plans to file a formal complaint against Dr. Toosi and the hospital over what happened. " The parents were forced to decide whether they should keep trying to resuscitate their son and the doctor provided them with false information ," stressed the attorney, who believes that what happened constitutes a serious lack of respect for human life.

For his part, the doctor's defense has expressed regret over the situation and wished the child a speedy recovery. " Dr. Toosi extends his sympathies to the young patient and his family, and wishes the child a speedy recovery ," it said in a statement in which he also reaffirmed his commitment to quality medical care. As for the hospital, it described what happened as " heartbreaking ," although it declined to offer details about the care provided to the minor for privacy reasons. " Patient safety and exceptional care are our highest priorities ," it said in a statement. The Prosecutor's Office had not yet made a decision on reviewing the case at the time this information was released.
The little boy suffers a severe brain injury and is recovering at home

The little boy's story has also been surrounded by controversy from the beginning. After the alleged drowning, Gilbert Police recommended filing child abuse charges against the parents, after both admitted they had lost sight of Vincent during a party held for the Super Bowl. According to the police report, they also admitted to having smoked marijuana that morning. Ultimately, Maricopa County Attorney Rachel Mitchell announced that no charges would be filed against Alexus Fiordilino and her husband.

Now, the family's main concern is the boy's health. Vincent suffers from a severe brain injury, cannot swallow, has seizures, and cannot sit up or crawl on his own, according to the information released about his condition. Despite the aftereffects, the little boy has been able to return home, where he continues recovering with his parents. His case has reopened the debate over the circumstances of his declaration of death and the possible responsibilities arising from what happened at the hospital.

articles.title: How Social Security benefits are calculated based on your lifetime earnings? This is how you can calculate them
articles.standfirst: The government uses decades of earnings to calculate benefits, and missing employment years may affect your monthly payment
articles.summary: The government uses decades of earnings to calculate benefits, and missing employment years may affect your monthly payment
articles.body:
A higher salary late in your career does not necessarily guarantee a significantly larger Social Security check. The amount you receive in retirement reflects decades of earnings, meaning decisions made long before leaving the workforce can affect your financial future.

The Social Security Administration (SSA) calculates retirement benefits using an individual's earnings history rather than simply considering their most recent salary or the total amount contributed through payroll taxes.

The system also rewards people who delay claiming benefits beyond their full retirement age, while reducing monthly payments for those who begin collecting earlier.

Understanding these calculations can help workers identify opportunities to increase their retirement income and avoid overlooking mistakes in their official earnings records.

Your 35 highest-earning years determine benefits

The calculation begins with the SSA reviewing earnings from employment covered by Social Security taxes throughout a worker's career.

Historical earnings are adjusted to account for changes in average national wages, allowing income earned decades ago to be compared with more recent salaries.

The agency then selects the worker's 35 highest-earning years and divides the combined adjusted earnings by 420 months.

This produces a figure known as Average Indexed Monthly Earnings , or AIME, which forms the foundation of the retirement benefit calculation.

However, employment gaps can make a substantial difference. Workers with fewer than 35 years of qualifying earnings have zero-income years included in their average.

Someone who worked for only 30 years, for example, would have five years counted as zero, potentially lowering their eventual monthly payment.

Lifetime earnings turned into monthly payments

After calculating AIME, the SSA applies a progressive formula to determine the Primary Insurance Amount , which is generally the benefit payable at full retirement age.

For workers first eligible in 2026, the calculation uses three earnings brackets:

90 percent of the first $1,286 in average indexed monthly earnings.

32 percent of earnings between $1,286 and $7,749.

15 percent of earnings above $7,749.

These thresholds, known as bend points, are adjusted annually to reflect changes in national wages.

The formula provides proportionally greater benefits to lower-income workers, although those with higher lifetime earnings generally receive larger monthly payments.

Claiming Social Security at 62 could mean smaller check

Even after the basic benefit is established, the age at which someone begins collecting Social Security can significantly influence their payment.

Americans can claim retirement benefits as early as age 62, but those born in 1960 or later face a 30 percent reduction if they claim five years before their full retirement age of 67.

Waiting until age 70 can instead increase monthly benefits to approximately 124 percent of the full retirement amount.

Continuing to work may also raise future payments when additional earnings replace lower-income years in the original calculation.

How to check your estimated Social Security benefits

Workers can review their earnings history and projected retirement payments through their personal my Social Security account.

The online service provides estimates based on recorded earnings and allows users to compare potential benefits at different claiming ages.

Annual cost-of-living adjustments can increase payments after retirement, while errors in employment records should be corrected promptly.

The important distinction is that Social Security benefits aren't determined by one particularly successful year. They reflect a lifetime of earnings, with the timing of retirement providing another opportunity to influence the final amount.

articles.title: Defying the 22nd Amendment: Trump Claims He Has a 'Right' to Run in 2028 Because 'They Cheated Me' in 2020
articles.standfirst: 'He has addressed the Constitutional Amendment that limits presidents to two terms: "I think the law says that I am not allowed to run again. I have studied that phrase..."'
articles.summary: 'He has addressed the Constitutional Amendment that limits presidents to two terms: "I think the law says that I am not allowed to run again. I have studied that phrase..."'
articles.body:
The President Donald Trump never ceases to surprise with his style of interpreting issues such as the one he has now brought up. Namely, whether he can run again in an election. During a campaign rally in Iowa ahead of the upcoming legislative elections, the leader suggested that he has the "right" to run for the presidency again in 2028 , arguing that the 2020 election was "stolen" from him and "rigged."

And it was then that he brought out all his heavy artillery by citing an example from the past. Trump addressed the Amendment to the U.S. Constitution that limits presidential terms to two . "I think the law says I'm not allowed to run again. I've studied that phrase ... Unfortunately , it's quite concise and there isn't much room for maneuver," the president initially acknowledged .

'But then, he has justified a possible candidacy by referring to his defeat against Joe Biden in 2020 : "They cheated us in the second one because we won three times. So I think I have the right to run again. I think I have the right to run again because they cheated. They rigged the election" .'

Contentious elections in the US in 2020

" State authorities and his own Department of Justice confirmed the election was clean and dismissed the allegations for lack of evidence, but Trump has always maintained that the results had been taken away from him.

The tension caused by that conflict rose even further when on January 6, 2021, the storming of the Capitol by a mob of his supporters took place, who violently broke into the seat of Congress in an attempt to stop the certification of Biden's victory.

articles.title: Sitting Bull, Legendary Native American Leader: “Let us put our minds together and see what life we can make for our children”
articles.standfirst: Sitting Bull was a pivotal figure in the Indians' resistance against the United States government in the 1800s.
articles.summary: Sitting Bull was a pivotal figure in the Indians' resistance against the United States government in the 1800s.
articles.body:
If you do a Google search of the most famous Native Americans in history, Sitting Bull is the name at the top of the list. Sitting Bull was a spiritual leader and chief for the Hunkpapa Lakota tribe, and became renowned for his efforts of resistance against the United States government and its new policies in the 1800s.

Sitting Bull was born sometime around 1831 . It's unclear exactly where he was born. Many believe it was along the Grand River in South Dakota , though his great-grandson once suggested he was born along the Yellowstone River in Montana . The first name given to him was actually " Jumping Badger ", and his nickname was " Slow " due to his careful nature. He was later named " Buffalo Bull Who Sits Down " by his father at 14 years old, but Americans commonly refer to him as Sitting Bull .

As he grew older, Sitting Bull became involved in conflicts with United States army parties and other tribes . His most famous conflict came in 1876 , dubbed the Battle of the Little Bighorn . The U.S. Army began treating those living off the Great Sioux Reservation , which included Sitting Bull's Lakota tribe. Thus began the Great Sioux War of 1876 .

The Battle of the Little Bighorn took place on June 25-26, 1876 in Montana. Sitting Bull had a vision of a Native American victory over the United States and their allied Crows and Arikaras tribes . Sitting Bull's vision came true, as the Lakota , Dakota , Northern Cheyenne , and Arapaho tribes handed their opponents a major defeat.

Sitting Bull was ultimately pressured out of the United States not long after, though. After being chased out due to not surrendering, as American military forces continued to cover more ground, Sitting Bull and his band went North to Canada . He remained in exile for four years, before returning to the United States in 1881 and surrendering .

He settled in the Standing Rock Reservation , then joined Buffalo Bill's Wild West show in the mid-1880s. In his mid-50s, U.S. agent James McLaughlin ordered Sitting Bull's arrest, out of fear he was soon to flee the reservation. A standoff took place on December 15, which resulted in bloodshed and the death of Sitting Bull via gunshot by Indian agency police at his home .

While many inspiring quotes from Sitting Bull continue to fortify his legacy, one stands out over the rest, due to his vision of the future: " Let us put our minds together and see what life we can make for our children ."

articles.title: Terrifying moment huge waves slam into a moving Amtrak train in California
articles.standfirst: The force of the ocean is raising new questions about the effects of an extreme climate phenomenon.
articles.summary: The force of the ocean is raising new questions about the effects of an extreme climate phenomenon.
articles.body:
This week, several videos captured one of the most striking scenes along the California coast: enormous waves slammed into an Amtrak passenger train as it traveled alongside the Pacific Ocean, covering its cars in sea foam. The footage quickly raised questions about what caused the powerful surf and how it relates to a Super Niño .

What does the Super Niño have to do with the huge waves?

Super Niño could play a role in what is happening across the Pacific. The phenomenon is characterized by unusually intense warming of surface waters , which can alter weather patterns and change storm activity in different regions.

When these changes affect ocean conditions, waves can grow stronger and reach exposed stretches of coastline. In San Clemente, California, the railroad tracks run alongside the shore, allowing waves to reach the rail infrastructure directly.

Why does the surf pose a risk to the tracks?

The danger does not end when the water recedes. Powerful waves can erode the ground and wash away the materials supporting the tracks , compromising the stability of the rail line and potentially disrupting train service.

With Super Niño conditions still a concern, changes in the Pacific will be key to understanding what could happen along the California coast in the coming months , particularly in areas where powerful surf threatens infrastructure built along the shoreline.

Eleven of the victims sustained gunshot wounds, and at least three victims sustained serious injuries, according to police.

The university said on social media that the shooting happened near its campus and that it remained safe.

articles.title: Breaking Katie Zacharia’s record: Britt McHenry’s 24-hour rise and fall at the Trump-era State Department
articles.standfirst: A same-day promotion turned into a swift departure after McHenry’s confrontation with spectators at a Washington Wizards game
articles.summary: A same-day promotion turned into a swift departure after McHenry’s confrontation with spectators at a Washington Wizards game
articles.body:
Britt McHenry’s latest career controversy has thrust the former ESPN reporter into the headlines again, this time following her brief stint in the Trump administration.

McHenry resigned from her position as a US State Department press adviser after a confrontation with spectators at an NBA game in Washington, DC, reportedly ending her government career just one day after receiving a promotion.

The incident occurred Wednesday night at Capital One Arena during a Washington Wizards game against the Milwaukee Bucks.

According to reports published by ABC News and Page Six, McHenry’s resignation followed footage showing her throwing a drink toward people in the stands before being escorted from the venue. The timing was particularly striking because she’d reportedly secured a significant career advancement earlier that same day.

A promotion overshadowed by a public confrontation

McHenry , 40, had joined the State Department the previous month as a press adviser covering Europe and Africa. Page Six reported that she was later promoted to lead External Affairs and Press for Under Secretary Jacob Helberg’s team.

However, the opportunity was short-lived, with a source telling the publication that she was forced to resign following the arena confrontation.

The dispute reportedly began when spectators made insulting comments about Milwaukee Bucks player Kyle Kuzma and his fiancée, model Winnie Harlow.

According to a source cited by Page Six, McHenry intervened and urged the hecklers to ease up. The situation subsequently escalated, with competing accounts emerging about what happened next.

A source claimed that spectators threw a drink at McHenry . However, video obtained by TMZ appears to show her throwing a drink toward people in the crowd as spectators chant for her to leave. She was then escorted from the stands, leaving amid boos and reportedly blowing kisses toward the crowd.

Although the footage captures part of the confrontation, it doesn't establish every detail of how the dispute began. A State Department spokesperson declined to comment on McHenry’s departure, describing it as an internal personnel matter.

The controversy has revived memories of McHenry’s previous professional setback, which also involved footage of her behavior becoming widely circulated online.

In 2015, ESPN suspended McHenry for one week after a video showed her berating an employee at a Washington towing company. Following her car’s removal, she launched into a series of personal insults, questioning the worker’s education, abilities and employment circumstances.

The clip attracted widespread criticism and became a defining controversy during her broadcasting career.

Her latest departure has drawn renewed attention to that earlier episode, creating uncomfortable parallels between her experiences in television and government communications. Both incidents involved public confrontations captured on video, although the circumstances surrounding each were different.

McHenry’s brief government tenure has therefore ended under a cloud of controversy, with her reported promotion quickly eclipsed by the arena incident. Rather than marking a new chapter in her career, the appointment has become notable for how abruptly it ended.

The dispute reportedly began when spectators made insulting comments about Milwaukee Bucks player Kyle Kuzma and his fiancée, model Winnie Harlow.
According to a source cited by Page Six, McHenry intervened and urged the hecklers to ease up. The situation subsequently escalated, with competing accounts emerging about what happened next.

A source claimed that spectators threw a drink at McHenry . However, video obtained by TMZ appears to show her throwing a drink toward people in the crowd as spectators chant for her to leave. She was then escorted from the stands, leaving amid boos and reportedly blowing kisses toward the crowd.

Although the footage captures part of the confrontation, it doesn't establish every detail of how the dispute began. A State Department spokesperson declined to comment on McHenry’s departure, describing it as an internal personnel matter.
The controversy has revived memories of McHenry’s previous professional setback, which also involved footage of her behavior becoming widely circulated online.

In 2015, ESPN suspended McHenry for one week after a video showed her berating an employee at a Washington towing company. Following her car’s removal, she launched into a series of personal insults, questioning the worker’s education, abilities and employment circumstances.
The clip attracted widespread criticism and became a defining controversy during her broadcasting career.

Her latest departure has drawn renewed attention to that earlier episode, creating uncomfortable parallels between her experiences in television and government communications. Both incidents involved public confrontations captured on video, although the circumstances surrounding each were different.

McHenry’s brief government tenure has therefore ended under a cloud of controversy, with her reported promotion quickly eclipsed by the arena incident. Rather than marking a new chapter in her career, the appointment has become notable for how abruptly it ended.

articles.title: Who is Pete Hegseth, the United States Secretary of Defense who has expelled trans people from the military
articles.standfirst: Some Navy and Marine Corps commanders have disobeyed the order and are looking for ways to keep the affected people in the ranks
articles.summary: Some Navy and Marine Corps commanders have disobeyed the order and are looking for ways to keep the affected people in the ranks
articles.body:
Pete Hegseth , an Army National Guard veteran with Bronze Star decorations for his deployments in Iraq and Afghanistan , first came to public attention mainly as a host on Fox News , a media outlet aligned with Donald Trump , before being appointed Secretary of Defense by the current President.

Known for his alignment with the hardline conservative wing and his critical stance against progressive policies within the Armed Forces , the head of the Pentagon restructured military policy under the premise that service should be reserved for those who meet traditional standards of physical and mental fitness . During a mass event before sailors and Marines, the secretary of Defense used a derogatory term to announce that he would expel transgender soldiers , pushing a strict bureaucratic review process to carry out their removal.

The Navy and the United States Marine Corps, against Pete Hegseth's decision

The directive designed by the Pentagon seemed inflexible: a mechanism whereby separation boards were required to process discharges without hesitation . To carry out the measure, extremely rigid instructions were issued under which board members were told to "circle certain words" that would certify a trans status in order to proceed with automatic dismissal. However, just a few steps from the auditorium where Hegseth spoke, at Quantico Base, the boards tasked with enforcing those orders were doing the opposite . What the Government had envisioned as a meteoric purge has run headlong into the troops' own judgment.

The ban argues that transgender people represent a costly burden on military effectiveness . However, the practical implementation in the Navy and the Marine Corps has taken an unexpected turn. Instead of meekly complying with the expulsion directives, the boards rebelled and voted in favor of allowing them to stay , prioritizing their colleagues' professional performance over ideological mandates. This phenomenon of veiled insubordination stands in sharp contrast to the pattern seen in the Army or the Air Force, where most hearings have resulted in immediate dismissals.

'The contradiction between the Pentagon's rhetoric and the reality of the military courts has become evident. While high-ranking officials point to diversity as an operational obstacle, in the Marines' hearings passionate defenses of group cohesion have emerged. In the case of Sergeant Damien Contreras , the review board decided to strike the clause on a history of hormone therapy from his findings sheet and include the phrase "remains qualified" in order to keep him on active duty, valuing his decade of impeccable service above the restrictions imposed by the administration.'

Legal experts and former military lawyers point out that this institutional brake reflects a deep sense of camaraderie. Former Air Force lawyer Rachel VanLandingham praised the judges' stance in The New York Times, noting that the boards are saying "they are not going to play that game" , refusing to endorse incoherent records or proceedings they consider outright unfair. This quiet resistance exposes a growing gap between the directives issued by the top brass and the values of loyalty on the front lines.

When the fulfillment of duty is above any directive: this is the devastating message

Although the number of favorable rulings is small and they could be overturned by politically appointed secretaries, the message sent by the Navy and the Marine Corps is devastating . In the Navy, where the percentage of diverse personnel is estimated to be higher than in other branches, career officers have argued that their subordinates have always carried out their duty impeccably. The troops are choosing to protect the effectiveness of their units rather than submit to arbitrary impositions.

The attempt to homogenize the armed forces through sweeping dismissals thus encounters an unexpected obstacle: the very judgment of military personnel who prioritize merit in the fulfillment of duty . In the Marine Corps, whose motto is Semper Fidelis, the respect earned after years of service and deployments carries more weight than the directives of a purge imposed from Pentagon offices.

articles.title: Nicki Minaj joins Trump at a rally on Air Force One and he praises her "beautiful ass": "It's hard not to notice it"
articles.standfirst: The artist has strengthened her ties with the American conservative movement and supports the president in every way she can
articles.summary: The artist has strengthened her ties with the American conservative movement and supports the president in every way she can
articles.body:
The relationship between Nicki Minaj and Donald Trump shows clear signs of great cordiality and affinity . The Trinidadian rapper accompanied the President of the United States aboard Air Force One this weekend on the way to a campaign event held in Michigan to support the Republican Senate candidate, Mike Rogers . Over the years, the artist has become one of his most visible supporters. Her support for the president has been reflected in various public appearances alongside members of the Republican Administration.

The latest sign of that closeness came through a video shared on X by Steven Cheung, White House communications director. In the footage, Minaj appears inside the presidential plane praising the policies promoted by Trump. " I think we've found the new White House press secretary," Cheung joked in the post. The singer responded to the comment with a laughing emoji.

Although Minaj did not speak at the rally, she did show her support with her presence, and it was Trump himself who wanted to make an aside about it. The president then made a striking remark by praising her "beautiful butt." "Stand up, it's hard not to see it," the president told the crowd.

Minaj has declared herself Trump's "number one fan"

The event had as its main objective to boost Mike Rogers's candidacy , who is facing Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in a closely contested race for a Senate seat. The upcoming midterm elections on November 3 will be key in determining control of the U.S. Congress.

In recent years, Minaj has strengthened her ties with the American conservative movement . The singer, who has millions of followers grouped under the name Barbz, has even gone so far as to declare herself Trump's "number one fan."

Minaj's brutal contrast with Trump over these years

The rapprochement is striking considering that in 2018 she harshly criticized the Republican's immigration policy and revealed that she had arrived in the United States irregularly when she was just five years old . Already in January of this year, she claimed to have received for free a "gold card" promoted by Trump , a controversial program linked to obtaining permanent residency for foreigners who make significant economic contributions to the U.S. government.

articles.title: Powerball Winning Numbers: Results for Monday, October 26 drawing for the $687 million jackpot
articles.standfirst: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $687 million for Monday night's drawing
articles.summary: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $687 million for Monday night's drawing
articles.body:
Lottery players across the United States are preparing for another chance to win a life-changing prize as Powerball returns on Monday, October 26, with an estimated jackpot of $687 million.

The drawing is scheduled for 10:59 p.m. Eastern Time, and the top prize has continued to grow after nobody matched all six numbers in Saturday's draw.

According to the official Powerball website, the jackpot's estimated cash value is $294.7 million before applicable taxes.

Monday's winning numbers have not yet been confirmed. The drawing will take place later tonight, meaning players should consult the official Powerball website once the results are published rather than rely on numbers from previous draws.

The growing prize offers another opportunity for ticket holders to dream of becoming multimillionaires. However, winning the jackpot requires matching all five white-ball numbers and the separate red Powerball number, making the odds extremely challenging.

What were the latest Powerball winning numbers?

The most recent completed drawing took place on Saturday, October 24, 2026. The winning numbers were 4, 5, 15, 19 and 55, with 19 as the Powerball .

The Power Play multiplier was 2X. No ticket matched all six numbers to claim the jackpot, allowing the estimated prize to increase to $687 million for Monday's draw.

Players waiting for Monday's results can check the official Powerball website after the drawing. The site publishes the winning combination, prize information and details about tickets that matched the required numbers.

Powerball drawings take place every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday at 10:59 p.m. ET. Tickets cost $2 per play, although players can add the Power Play feature for an additional $1. This option can multiply eligible non-jackpot prizes, but it does not increase the jackpot itself.

The jackpot winner can choose between an annuity paid through 30 graduated payments over 29 years or a lump-sum cash payment.

The advertised jackpot and cash value are estimates before federal and applicable local taxes, so the amount a winner ultimately receives may be considerably lower.

How difficult is it to win the $687 million jackpot?

Powerball's jackpot odds are approximately 1 in 292.2 million, according to lottery information published by participating state lotteries. The overall odds of winning any prize are around 1 in 24.9.

Players must select five white-ball numbers from 1 to 69 and one red Powerball number from 1 to 26. They can choose their own combination or ask a lottery terminal to generate a random selection.

Matching fewer numbers can still produce a prize, with payouts depending on the combination matched and whether the ticket includes Power Play. The jackpot, however, requires all six numbers to be correct.

For anyone holding a ticket for Monday's drawing, the important step is to wait for the official results and check the numbers carefully.

Because the October 26 drawing has yet to take place, the winning combination and whether anyone claims the $687 million prize remain unknown.

The next scheduled drawing after Monday is Wednesday, October 28, at 10:59 p.m. ET. If nobody wins the jackpot on Monday, the prize is expected to roll over and grow again, although the next advertised amount will depend on ticket sales and official lottery estimates.
